column1: # Mutations that the test suite must catch.
# These are written by hand, and they are the half a generator cannot produce.
# swift-mutants reads this package and makes 2256 of its own - comparison flips,
# boolean literals, arithmetic, connective operands - and measuring both against
# each other showed that only 20 of the 290 here are among them. The rest ask a
# A generated mutant asks whether an operator is correct. These ask whether a
# piece of code is load-bearing: drop the tie-break from a sort, remove a guard
# clause, use the wrong named constant, take an argument out of a call, collapse
# a ternary, return the value instead of the value passed through a function.
# Every hole worth having found in this project came from a question of the
# second kind, and none of them is an operator flip.
# They also cover the one place swift-mutants currently cannot reach. Its guard
# is injected as a private function, which an @inlinable function may not call,
# so every mutant inside one is refused - and this package marks its innermost
# geometry @inlinable. Geo.swift and Direction16.swift hold the predicates the
# whole solver rests on, and the eight rows here that name them are, for now,
# the only mutation coverage they have.
# A column may not be empty and may not contain a newline. Reading the file
# splits on tabs, and consecutive tabs collapse into one - so an empty column
# silently shifts every column after it, and the mutation then replaces the
# anchor with its own description. That does not compile, a mutant that does not
# compile counts as killed, and the row passes for a reason nobody intended.
# To delete a line, replace it with something inert rather than with nothing.
# Columns are tab-separated: file, exact search text (must appear exactly once),
# Only list mutations that genuinely change behaviour. An "equivalent mutant"
# produces identical output for every input and will always survive; listing one
# just pressures you into contorting the tests. Four have been tried and removed
#   - relaxing the well-formed guard before building the saliency layer: the
#     map's own subscript already answers zero for a malformed map, so every
#   - falling back to an empty buffer when a picture is missing: converting an
#     empty buffer fails, so the same warning is reported either way.
#   - relaxing `guard scale != 1` in the coordinate conversion: dividing by one
#     is what the guard was skipping.
#   - relaxing `guard width > 0` in overlapArea: a zero width multiplies out to zero.
#   - relaxing the clipped-interval guard in segmentIntersectsInterior: the strict
#     midpoint containment check already rejects those cases.
#   - `b.minX > a.maxX` to `>=` in gapSquared: when the rectangles touch, both
#     branches yield a delta of exactly zero.
#   - turning either early exit in the Liang-Barsky clipper into a continue: those
#     branches only fire when the slab intersection is already empty, and the
#     midpoint check cannot then report a false positive. A search over two million
#     random segments plus a dense grid found no distinguishing input for either
#     branch, matching the proof written up above segmentIntersectsInterior.
